messages:
Sam: FYI - customer ACME reporting sudden p99 request latency spike (~3-5x) across eu1 after last night's infra updates. They see it in realtime ingestion and embeddings. Escalating to infra.
Priya: Thanks Sam. Any correlation with the kernel/driver rollout window?
Sam: yes - rollout started 2025-11-02 02:10 UTC, ACME spike first noticed ~02:45 UTC. Attaching quick metrics: 
```
api_p99: 240ms -> 1.2s
nvme_util: 72% -> 94%
kv_cache_misses: +180%
```
Jordan: Can you paste a short `dmesg` and `iostat -x 1 3` from one affected node? Also which model route is hot?
Sam: Pasting snippets below (redacted node id).
```
[Nov 02 02:43:17] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x3ff timed out, aborting
[Nov 02 02:43:18] nvme nvme0: admin queue timeout
```
```
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s  rkB/s wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgrq-merge await r_await w_await aqu-sz svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00  0.00  5.00 120.00  400.00  9600.00  82.67    0.00   9.20   0.40  9.48   1.20  0.08  92.00
```
Priya: nvme timeouts + high util lines up. That can blow up tail latency for KV cache reads which our runtime depends on. Is this a CUDA/driver + kernel combo rollout?
Tom: Yes, we pushed kernel v6.4.18 + NVIDIA driver 540.23 last night to eu1 as part of the scheduled patch window. We saw some degraded NVMe latencies in lab with specific firmware combos but rolled anyway.
Jordan: Hypothesis: new kernel I/O scheduler interaction + driver-level I/O patterns (unbuffered, small random reads) caused queue buildup on nvme controller -> high latencies on hot KV paths -> p99 API regressions.
Kai: Quick mitigations we can try: 1) route ACME traffic off eu1 to eu2 fallback pool (low-friction). 2) Temporarily set model route to smaller variant (reduce KV hot lookups). 3) Rollback driver on a canary subset.
Sam: ACME ops asked for timeline - can we do routing now?
Priya: I'm initiating route-level fallback to eu2 for ACME by adding a routing override (5m canary) and enabling degraded-model for embeddings. @deploy-bot can you confirm rollout?
deploy-bot: Scheduled routing override for customer=ACME -> eu2 (weight=100%) at 1881234670, TTL=00:20:00.
Tom: On infra, I'm preparing a targeted rollback of NVIDIA driver on 3 affected hosts to validate repro. If rollback gives stable nvme latency we proceed cluster-wide.
Jordan: Also let's toggle `nvme_core.io_timeout` and `nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us`? Be cautious - prefer rollback first.
Priya: For observability: increased kv_cache latency alert to trigger at 500ms for next 6h and added a dashboard panel with per-node nvme queue depth.
Kai: Customer update prepared: "We observed an infrastructure interaction after last night's maintenance causing temporary storage latency in eu1. We've routed your traffic to an alternate region and are mitigating while we investigate. Expect follow-up within 2 hours."
Sam: ACME acknowledged and appreciates fast routing.
Tom: Rollback on the 3 hosts done (nodes: eu1-41, eu1-42, eu1-47). Early telemetry: nvme util down to 58%, p99 API ~210ms -> 320ms. Looks promising.
Priya: Good. Plan: 1) Hold rollout of 540.23 in eu1 for now. 2) Re-run driver+kernel test matrix in staging with current nvme firmware (fw 2.3.1). 3) If safe, reintroduce with io-tuning knobs (adjust qdepth, cgroup io weight) and gradual canary. 4) For customer-facing resilience, add route fallback policy that activates on host-io-alerts.
Jordan: I'll create a repro runbook: steps to reproduce locally (1- enable high concurrent small-random reads against kvcache, 2- apply kernel+driver combo, 3- monitor nvme qdepth + dmesg). Will attach logs.
Kai: Anything else before we close this thread?
Sam: I'll keep monitoring ACME traffic and will post final status once we sign off rollback testing. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Priya: Marking incident as active-investigation. Follow-up doc + timelines in #incidents-postmortems.
Sam: Closing the Slack loop here, will update the ticket after the staged test completes.
